svg.aria-label: How to write 看: 9 strokes · 8 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 看
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 看 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 看.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E7%9C%8B.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 看. Medians 1–4 form the upper hand-like element; medians 5–9 complete 目 below. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order and that the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus preserves that ordered sequence while fitting its learner pen paths to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline, whose width and proportions differ from the Arphic-derived source graphics.
